articles.headline: Wheeler fans 7 straight to open game, Stott hits tiebreaking RBI single as Phillies beat Brewers 6-4
articles.description: — Zack Wheeler struck 11, including a franchise-record seven in a row to start the game, Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking RBI single with two out in the eighth inning and the Philadelphia Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Zack Wheeler struck 11, including a franchise-record seven in a row to start the game, Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking RBI single with two out in the eighth inning and the Philadelphia Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night.


              Brandon Marsh homered, doubled and drove in three runs for Philadelphia, which began play holding the final NL wild-card spot with a four-game cushion over Arizona.


              William Contreras had three RBI for NL Central-leading Milwaukee. The Brewers needed a win over Philadelphia or loss by the Braves to Cincinnati on Tuesday to clinch a bye in the wild-card round and earn home-field advantage for the NLDS.


              After the Brewers scored twice in the sixth off Wheeler to tie the game at 3, Stott singled to center off Colton Gordon (0-1). Garrett Mitchell’s throw went to third base to try to get Alec Bohm running from first. But the ball ricocheted off Bohm’s foot, and both he and Luis Arraez scored to make it 5-3. 


              Jhoan Duran earned his 33rd save after José Alvarado (5-3) got the final out of the eighth.


              Wheeler was unhittable at the outset and had sights on Pablo López’s MLB record of nine K’s in a row to open a contest before Cooper Pratt grounded out to third base for the second out of the third inning. Watching Wheeler from the dugout was teammate Aaron Nola, who has a share of the MLB record with 10 consecutive strikeouts of the Mets in 2021. 


              The Phillies began Tuesday trailing the Padres and Cubs by one game for the top spot in the NL wild card. Philadelphia holds the tiebreaker over San Diego but not Chicago.


              The Brewers dropped to 13-6 this month and were not able to extend their franchise record of 98 wins, set in Sunday’s 3-0 victory at Baltimore. 


              Up next
              Brewers RHP Logan Henderson (10-3, 2.51 ERA) opposes Phillies RHP Aaron Nola (7-10, 4.49) in the second game of the three-game series on Wednesday night.


              ------


              AP MLB: https://apnews.com/hub/mlb

articles.headline: CJ Abrams homers twice, drives in three runs as Nationals beat Tigers 3-1
articles.description: — CJ Abrams hit a tiebreaking two-run homer and added a solo shot to give the Washington Nationals a 3-1 victory over the Detroit Tigers on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- — CJ Abrams hit a tiebreaking two-run homer and added a solo shot to give the Washington Nationals a 3-1 victory over the Detroit Tigers on Tuesday night.


              The Nationals won for the seventh time in 10 games, while Detroit dropped to 2-5 in its last seven. The Tigers have scored exactly one run in all five losses, while scoring nine and 11 runs in the two wins.


              Both teams are 74-84 with four games left in the season.


              Jackson Kent (2-4) picked up the win in relief of Nationals opener Riley Cornelio. Kent pitched four innings, allowing one unearned run on six hits and two walks. Erik Tolman pitched the ninth for his fourth save.


              Tigers starter Drew Anderson (5-7) took the loss, allowing three runs on five hits. He struck out five without walking a batter.


              Washington took a 1-0 lead in the second on a long homer to right-center field by Abrams. That gave him 100 RBI to go along with his 30 homer/30 stolen base season.


              The Tigers tied the game in the sixth when Ben Malgeri scored on Kent's second wild pitch of the inning. Washington also missed two opportunities to turn double plays in the inning.


              Abrams then hit a two-run homer in the seventh, his 33rd of the season, to end Anderson's night. 


              Up next
              The teams finish their three-game series on Wednesday afternoon with Tigers LHP Framber Valdez (10-11, 4.06) facing a yet-to-be-announced Nationals starter.


              ------

articles.headline: Woman says she reported alleged 49ers impersonator to team in December
articles.description: A woman who says she is a victim in the FBI's fraud case against Daejon Love said she sent a "complaint/concern" to the Niners in December 2025, eight months before Love was arrested and charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
articles.headlineJa: 49ers関係者を装ったとされる人物について、女性が12月にチームに通報したと語る
articles.descriptionJa: デイジョン・ラブに対するFBIの詐欺事件の被害者であると主張する女性は、ラブが電信詐欺および電信詐欺の共謀罪で逮捕・起訴される8か月前の2025年12月に、49ersに「苦情・懸念」を送ったと述べた。
articles.body:
A woman who says she is a victim in the FBI's fraud case against Daejon Love, a man who is accused of impersonating a San Francisco 49ers player, told ESPN on Tuesday that she submitted a complaint about him via the team's website in December, eight months before he was arrested.

Gwen Herndon said she sent a "complaint/concern" form submission to the Niners on Dec. 20, 2025. According to her message, which was reviewed by ESPN, Herndon wrote that "there is a federal investigation surrounding a man pretending to be a 49ers player," naming Love, and saying he stole money from women and that "he is severely damaging the reputation of your team."

"I wanted you to be aware of the situation and hopefully proactive in denouncing his involvement on your team," she wrote in the message.

In the email exchange provided by Herndon, she received a response from a general Levi's Stadium guest services account a week later on Dec. 27, 2025.

"We take reports of individuals misrepresenting themselves as members of the San Francisco 49ers very seriously," the response said. "For safety and legal reasons, the team cannot comment on ongoing investigations or specific individuals. However, we appreciate you bringing this to our attention and encouraging proactive measures to protect the integrity of the organization.

"If you have information that could assist law enforcement or legal authorities, we encourage you to contact the appropriate agencies directly. Our internal team will also monitor any instances of impersonation and take action as appropriate to protect fans and the team's reputation. Thank you again for your vigilance and concern for the Niners community," the email said.

Herndon said she had no further contact with the 49ers after the email response in December. It's unclear whether anyone at the Niners reviewed the email Herndon said she sent. A Niners team source told ESPN last week that the team had not received any reports about Love before it was contacted by the FBI in August.

On Tuesday, a 49ers spokesperson declined to confirm the email's existence or to provide further comment on the email, citing the FBI's ongoing investigation.

Love and his alleged partner in the scheme, Taylor Chan, were arrested Aug. 24 and charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Federal authorities said the duo defrauded more than two dozen women out of about $1.3 million.

Love would meet women via dating apps, falsely portray himself as a "legitimately wealthy" 49ers player or real estate investor and solicit money from them, the FBI said. According to federal court filings, Love was wearing 49ers apparel when he was arrested in Boise, Idaho, and "the FBI later learned from interviews that Love was in Boise as part of his scheme and was actively defrauding three more victims in Idaho."

articles.headline: Jones takes perfect game into the 6th, Pirates top Cardinals 2-0 for 5th straight win
articles.description: — Jared Jones allowed one hit over seven dominant innings and the Pittsburgh Pirates inched closer to the franchise's first winning season in eight years with a 2-0 win over St. Louis on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- — Jared Jones allowed one hit over seven dominant innings and the Pittsburgh Pirates inched closer to the franchise's first winning season in eight years with a 2-0 win over St. Louis on Tuesday night.


              The hard-throwing Jones (5-6) retired the first 16 batters he faced before Nathan Church's bloop landed just beyond the outstretched glove of Pirates third baseman Jacob Gonzalez with one out in the sixth. Church sprinted to second for a double but remained there after Masyn Wynn lined out and J.J. Wetherholt struck out to end the inning.


              Jones, who returned from Tommy John surgery in late May, tied a season high with nine strikeouts in seven innings and improved to 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in four starts in September. Gregory Soto worked around a leadoff walk to record his 16th save.


              Ryan O'Hearn delivered an RBI-single for the Pirates and rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin had two hits for Pittsburgh, and Bryan Reynolds added his major league-leading 40th double. The Pirates have won five straight to improve to 80-77 with five games remaining. Pittsburgh is seeking its first winning campaign since going 82-79 in 2018.


              Andre Pallant (12-8) nearly matched Jones pitch for pitch in six innings of work. The right-hander's only hiccup came in the sixth, when Oneil Cruz walked with one out, moved to second on a fielder's choice and scored on O'Hearn's sharp single to left. Pallant is just 2-2 in 10 starts since the All-Star break despite pitching to a 3.00 ERA over that span. 


              The Cardinals fell to 76-81 with the loss. If St. Louis doesn't win out, the franchise will experience consecutive losing seasons for the first time since 1958 and 1959, the second-longest stretch between consecutive losing years in the history of major North American professional sports.


              Up next
              The series continues on Wednesday. Matthew Liberatore (5-14, 5.36 ERA) gets the start for the Cardinals. The Pirates have yet to announce a starter in what is likely a bullpen game.


              ------

articles.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Walker, Shough on the rise while Maye, McConkey fall
articles.description: Need a quick free agent pickup -- or roster overhaul -- after Week 2? These rankings are designed to help.
articles.headlineJa: 残りシーズンのランキング：ウォーカーとショウが上昇、メイとマコンキーは下落
articles.descriptionJa: 第2週を終えてフリーエージェントの補強やロースターの刷新が必要ですか？このランキングがその手助けとなります。
articles.body:
Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize the players for their future potential and/or to gauge their value in trade. Eric's top 100 can be found below the positions in this column. 

Quarterback

Rankings changes: Wow. Serious injuries to the top two selections from the 2024 draft and a late 2025 first-rounder are the story, as fantasy managers will miss the Bears' Caleb Williams (hamstring), Commanders' Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Giants' Jaxson Dart (knee) for an undetermined length of time. Each was among our top 10 QBs. Perhaps the mercurial Williams will return far sooner, so he remains in QB2 range in these rankings, but the risk of reinjury is high. Dart might be lost for the season. Backups Jameis Winston and Marcus Mariota enter the rankings, and they might be playing for months.

With three passers dropping in the rankings, nearly everyone else rises. The 49ers' Brock Purdy, Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes, Saints' Tyler Shough and Lions' Jared Goff are all in the top 10. The Panthers' Bryce Young rises into safer QB2 territory, with room for more. The Patriots' Drake Maye, last year's No. 2 QB scorer, remains in the top 10, but perhaps not for long after two disappointing outings totaling 17.84 points. The Rams' Matthew Stafford rebounds from Australia and is No. 11. It is quite amazing how quickly fantasy value changes in the NFL.

Running back

Rankings changes: Volume is king, and no running back earned more in Week 2 than the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III. Will he stay healthy? That was an offseason concern, but so far he looks awesome and he continues rising into the top 10. For those who want Walker at No. 1 ... c'mon, we are not there yet. Walker versus Bijan Robinson? It feels premature, though Robinson does drop a spot behind Jonathan Taylor to No. 3. Praise Walker, but if a Robinson investor offers him for Walker, do it.

Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is among the big risers at running back, though we lack confirmation of solid volume moving ahead (same with the Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson). The Buccaneers' Bucky Irving and Panthers' Chuba Hubbard rise to RB2 status, as their reported timeshares appear to be rather one-sided. Aaron Jones Sr. is healthy and seeing volume. Don't forget about the Saints' Alvin Kamara and Seahawks' Zach Charbonnet, and watch for injury updates on the Eagles' Saquon Barkley.

Wide receiver

Rankings changes: Many star receivers delivered in Week 2, but the rankings movement at this position happened in the late WR2 range, as the Panthers' Jalen Coker, Packers' Christian Watson, Broncos' Jaylen Waddle, Jaguars' Parker Washington and Browns' Denzel Boston continue to add value. Perhaps they catch some early underachievers such as the Falcons' Drake London and Cowboys' George Pickens soon. They have already passed the Chargers' Ladd McConkey and Lions' Jameson Williams.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA offseason trade grades: Finney-Smith, Schroder, more deals
articles.description: We're grading the biggest NBA trades of the offseason, including the Atlanta deal that sent Hield and Nembhard to Charlotte for Finney-Smith.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, with Aaron Wiggins' trade to the Atlanta Hawks on June 22 the first move in what has already been a frenzied offseason.

The big news came a day before the NBA draft, when Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded by the Milwaukee Bucks to the Miami Heat in a blockbuster. There was another big trade the morning after the draft, as the Charlotte Hornets shipped LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves. And the trades haven't stopped since.

I'm grading every trade this offseason, including draft deals, and breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the on-court impact and ages of involved players, the cost in terms of draft picks and future financial implications, and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win the championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Latest buzz | FA signing grades | Trade machine

Depth charts | Offseason guides | Draft coverage

Sept. 22: Hawks send Hield, Nembhard to Hornets for Finney-Smith

Charlotte Hornets get: G Buddy Hield, G Ryan Nembhard, cash considerations

Atlanta Hawks get: F Dorian Finney-Smith

Grade for Hawks: B+

For the Hawks, this swap of reserve wings is primarily about resolving a roster crunch, as they trade two players -- including backup guard Nembhard, whom they had initially acquired alongside Luguentz Dort in an earlier trade -- for one.

That fix comes at a minor price, as Finney-Smith will earn $14.2 million this season, compared with $11.8 million combined for Hield and Nembhard. (Finney-Smith and Hield are both nominally signed for additional years, but for zero guaranteed money.) The Hawks are reportedly sending cash to Charlotte in this deal, as well.

But this deal is smart business for the Hawks because it gives them another potential two-way contributor on the wing, as they build out a fearsome defensive rotation. Hield doesn't fit that mold, and he never seemed to find his footing in Atlanta. He arrived from Golden State in the Kristaps Porzingis trade last February but played just 51 minutes over the rest of the regular season, as the Hawks enjoyed their late-season surge without him.

Finney-Smith, meanwhile, was far worse than Hield last season, as he averaged only 3.3 points per game and made 27% of his 3s after returning from ankle surgery. That disappointing level of production incentivized Houston to trade him to Charlotte earlier this offseason, in a salary dump that brought the Hornets three second-round picks.

articles.headline: Hawks trade Hield, Nembhard to Hornets for Finney-Smith
articles.description: The Hawks are sending Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith.
articles.headlineJa: ホークスがヒールドとネムハードをホーネッツにトレード、フィニー＝スミスを獲得
articles.descriptionJa: ホークスはバディ・ヒールド、ライアン・ネムハード、および金銭補償をシャーロット・ホーネッツに放出し、ドリアン・フィニー＝スミスを獲得する。
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks are trading Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash considerations to the Charlotte Hornets for Dorian Finney-Smith, the team announced on Tuesday. 

The Hornets are expected to waive Nembhard as part of the trade, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The Hawks create a $2.1 million trade exception and the Hornets likely create a $4.5 million trade exception with the deal, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

Hield landed in Atlanta in the trade that sent Kristaps Porzingis to the Golden State Warriors but appeared in just seven games for the Hawks last season; the sharpshooting guard is due around $9.5 million this season and has a player option for just over $10 million for 2027-28.

 

Finney-Smith was acquired by Charlotte in a trade with the Houston Rockets earlier in the offseason. The veteran wing missed the first two months of the season for Houston and has three years left on his $53 million contract, including a player option for 2028-29.

Nembhard, an undrafted rookie last season for Dallas, was acquired by the Hawks in a three-team trade that sent Zaccharie Risacher to the Mavericks and Luguentz Dort back to Atlanta from Oklahoma City.

Nembhard, 23, averaged 6.6 points and 5.3 assists in 19.5 minutes per game last season.
